note: The last nine scouted addresses never mailed, all UK and Irish institutions holding trees we publish. Hidde, 2026-09-08: 'doe die laatste 9 maar'. Every photograph claim checked against the data before writing: two candidate records overstated the gap (the Cheapside Plane and the Great Sycamore both have approved photos) and the mails say what is actually missing.

mails.subject: Can you help me with ancienttrees.app? Three trees on your grounds
mails.body:
Hi,

Three of our Irish entries stand on OPW ground: Queen Victoria's Sequoia at Aras an Uachtarain, the Great Sycamore of Farmleigh, and the 1870 Campbell's magnolia in Fota Arboretum. Here is the sycamore: https://ancienttrees.app/dublin/great-sycamore-of-farmleigh

My name is Hidde. I love old trees and being outdoors, and with ancienttrees.app I try to get more people to appreciate nature and go outside. It is live with about 2,800 trees in more than 500 places, and the iOS app launched last week: https://apps.apple.com/nl/app/ancient-trees/id6806177833?l=en-GB

Two things would help. We have no photograph of Queen Victoria's Sequoia, and if you have one we could use, credited however you ask, it would finish that page. And if we have anything wrong about the three, I would rather hear it from you than leave it up.

Is there a tree on OPW ground you would point a visitor to that we have missed?

Thanks,
Hidde

mails.org: National Botanic Gardens of Ireland, Glasnevin
mails.subject: Can you help me with ancienttrees.app? Six Glasnevin trees
mails.body:
Hi,

Six of our seventeen Dublin trees are in your gardens, from the dawn redwood to the tree of heaven we call Ireland's largest. https://ancienttrees.app/dublin/irelands-largest-tree-of-heaven

My name is Hidde. I love old trees and being outdoors, and with ancienttrees.app I try to get more people to appreciate nature and go outside. It is live with about 2,800 trees in more than 500 places, and the iOS app launched last week: https://apps.apple.com/nl/app/ancient-trees/id6806177833?l=en-GB

Not one of the six has a photograph, which is a shame on the best set of trees we have in Ireland. If you have images we could use, credited however you ask, I would use them. And tell me if we have any of the six wrong.

Which tree in the gardens would you send a first-time visitor to?

Thanks,
Hidde
